faq.question: How much does window replacement cost in Benicia?
faq.answer: Benicia homeowners typically invest $5,000 to $11,500 for a full window replacement project. Homes in the historic First Street district often require custom sizing to match original Victorian and Italianate profiles, which can add to project cost. Standard replacement in newer neighborhoods starts around $450 per window installed.

faq.question: Do I need a permit to replace windows in Benicia?
faq.answer: Yes. Benicia requires a building permit for window replacements. Properties in the First Street Corridor or other designated historic areas may also need review from the Historic Preservation Review Commission to ensure new windows are architecturally compatible with the building's historic character. Our team manages all permit applications on your behalf.

faq.question: Is it worth replacing 20-year-old windows in Benicia?
faq.answer: Often yes. Twenty-year-old windows in Benicia commonly show fogged glass, drafts and weak locks. Newer ENERGY STAR units improve comfort and curb appeal; Deluxe Windows compares payback against your utility rates and home style before recommending replacement.

faq.question: Should I choose fiberglass or vinyl windows in Benicia?
faq.answer: Vinyl is the value pick for most Benicia replacements and handles Bay Area weather well. Fiberglass (including Marvin Ultrex) is stronger, more stable in temperature swings and better for larger openings or coastal exposure. We show both side by side in the showroom and on-site.

faq.question: How long does window replacement take in Benicia?
faq.answer: Most Benicia projects are measured in one visit and installed in one to three working days once products arrive — typically four to eight weeks after ordering, depending on brand and custom sizes.
